Train Validation Test Split¶

Splitting Driver Aware data into Train Val Test Split¶

In [9]:
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupShuffleSplit

# load the driver mapping again for clarity
csv_path = "/Users/linux/Desktop/AI Y3 S2/Computer Vision/Coursework/Dataset/driver_imgs_list.csv"
driver_df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)

# build the full image path for each row
train_dir = "/Users/linux/Desktop/AI Y3 S2/Computer Vision/Coursework/Dataset/train"
driver_df["image_path"] = driver_df.apply(
    lambda row: os.path.join(train_dir, row["classname"], row["img"]), axis=1
)

# first split: 80 percent drivers for train, 20 percent for temp (val + test)
gss1 = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
train_idx, temp_idx = next(gss1.split(driver_df, groups=driver_df["subject"]))

train_df = driver_df.iloc[train_idx].reset_index(drop=True)
temp_df = driver_df.iloc[temp_idx].reset_index(drop=True)

# second split: split the remaining 20 percent in half, 10 percent val, 10 percent test
gss2 = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.5, random_state=42)
val_idx, test_idx = next(gss2.split(temp_df, groups=temp_df["subject"]))

val_df = temp_df.iloc[val_idx].reset_index(drop=True)
test_df = temp_df.iloc[test_idx].reset_index(drop=True)

# to confirm no driver overlap between sets
train_drivers = set(train_df["subject"].unique())
val_drivers = set(val_df["subject"].unique())
test_drivers = set(test_df["subject"].unique())

print("Train images:", len(train_df), "| Drivers:", len(train_drivers))
print("Val images:", len(val_df), "| Drivers:", len(val_drivers))
print("Test images:", len(test_df), "| Drivers:", len(test_drivers))

print("\nOverlap check (should all be empty sets):")
print("Train and Val overlap:", train_drivers & val_drivers)
print("Train and Test overlap:", train_drivers & test_drivers)
print("Val and Test overlap:", val_drivers & test_drivers)

Preprocessing and DataLoaders¶

Defining Image Transformations¶

In [10]:
# imagenet normalization stats since model 3 will use a pretrained resnet
imagenet_mean = [0.485, 0.456, 0.406]
imagenet_std = [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]

# training transform includes light augmentation
# no horizontal flip here, since flipping would turn texting right into texting left
train_transform = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize((224, 224)),
    transforms.RandomRotation(15),
    transforms.ColorJitter(brightness=0.3, contrast=0.3, saturation=0.2),
    transforms.RandomAffine(degrees=0, translate=(0.1, 0.1), scale=(0.9, 1.1)),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize(mean=imagenet_mean, std=imagenet_std),
    transforms.RandomErasing(p=0.3, scale=(0.02, 0.1)),
])

# validation and test transform has no augmentation, just resize and normalize
eval_transform = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize((224, 224)),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize(mean=imagenet_mean, std=imagenet_std)
])

print("Transforms Defined")

Transforms Defined

Custom Dataset Class¶

In [11]:
class DriverBehaviorDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, dataframe, transform):
        self.dataframe = dataframe.reset_index(drop=True)
        self.transform = transform

        # merging the original 10 classes down to 4 behaviour groups
        # c0 safe driving  + c9 talking passenger                      -> Safe / Talking
        # c1 texting right + c2 phone right + c3 texting left + c4 phone left -> Using Phone
        # c5 radio         + c6 drinking                               -> Distracted Driving
        # c7 reaching behind + c8 hair makeup                          -> Reaching / Grooming
        self.class_to_idx = {
            "c0": 0, "c9": 0,
            "c1": 1, "c2": 1, "c3": 1, "c4": 1,
            "c5": 2, "c6": 2,
            "c7": 3, "c8": 3,
        }

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.dataframe)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        row = self.dataframe.iloc[idx]
        img_path = row["image_path"]
        label = self.class_to_idx[row["classname"]]

        image = Image.open(img_path).convert("RGB")
        image = self.transform(image)

        return image, label

print("Dataset Class Defined")

Dataset Class Defined

Model 1: The Baseline CNN¶

Defining Baseline CNN Architecture¶

In [13]:
class BaselineCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=4):
        super(BaselineCNN, self).__init__()

        # block 1: 3 input channels (rgb) to 16 feature maps
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.pool1 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        # block 2: 16 to 32 feature maps
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.pool2 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        # block 3: 32 to 64 feature maps
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.pool3 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        self.relu = nn.ReLU()

        # after 3 poolings, 224 becomes 28 (224 / 2 / 2 / 2)
        # flattened size is 64 channels times 28 times 28
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(64 * 28 * 28, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool1(self.relu(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.pool2(self.relu(self.conv2(x)))
        x = self.pool3(self.relu(self.conv3(x)))

        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)  # flatten

        x = self.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.fc2(x)

        return x

print("Baseline CNN Architecture Defined.")

Baseline CNN Architecture Defined.

Reusable Training Function¶

In [14]:
def train_model(model, train_loader, val_loader, device, num_epochs=10, lr=0.001):
    model = model.to(device)

    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)

    history = {"train_loss": [], "val_loss": [], "train_acc": [], "val_acc": []}

    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        # training phase
        model.train()
        running_loss = 0.0
        correct = 0
        total = 0

        for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} train"):
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)

            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            total += labels.size(0)

        train_loss = running_loss / total
        train_acc = correct / total

        # validation phase
        model.eval()
        val_running_loss = 0.0
        val_correct = 0
        val_total = 0

        with torch.no_grad():
            for images, labels in val_loader:
                images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
                outputs = model(images)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

                val_running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
                _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
                val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
                val_total += labels.size(0)

        val_loss = val_running_loss / val_total
        val_acc = val_correct / val_total

        history["train_loss"].append(train_loss)
        history["val_loss"].append(val_loss)
        history["train_acc"].append(train_acc)
        history["val_acc"].append(val_acc)

        print(f"epoch {epoch+1}: train loss {train_loss:.4f}, train acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
              f"val loss {val_loss:.4f}, val acc {val_acc:.4f}")

    return model, history

print("Training Function Defined.")

Training Function Defined.

Model 2: Improved CNN¶

Defining Improved CNN Architecture¶

In [17]:
class ImprovedCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=4, dropout_rate=0.3):
        super(ImprovedCNN, self).__init__()

        # block 1
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(16)
        self.pool1 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        # block 2
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(32)
        self.pool2 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        # block 3
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.pool3 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)

        # after 3 poolings, 224 becomes 28
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(64 * 28 * 28, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool1(self.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x))))
        x = self.pool2(self.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x))))
        x = self.pool3(self.relu(self.bn3(self.conv3(x))))

        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)  # flatten

        x = self.dropout(x)  # dropout before fully connected layers
        x = self.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.dropout(x)  # dropout again before final classification
        x = self.fc2(x)

        return x

Improved CNN Architecture Defined.

Updating Training Function with Optimiser Choice¶

In [19]:
def train_model_v2(model, train_loader, val_loader, device, num_epochs, lr, optimizer_name):
    model = model.to(device)

    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    if optimizer_name == "adam":
        optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)
    elif optimizer_name == "sgd":
        optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=lr, momentum=0.9)
    else:
        raise ValueError("unsupported optimizer name")

    history = {"train_loss": [], "val_loss": [], "train_acc": [], "val_acc": []}

    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        model.train()
        running_loss = 0.0
        correct = 0
        total = 0

        for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs} train"):
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)

            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            total += labels.size(0)

        train_loss = running_loss / total
        train_acc = correct / total

        model.eval()
        val_running_loss = 0.0
        val_correct = 0
        val_total = 0

        with torch.no_grad():
            for images, labels in val_loader:
                images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
                outputs = model(images)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

                val_running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
                _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
                val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
                val_total += labels.size(0)

        val_loss = val_running_loss / val_total
        val_acc = val_correct / val_total

        history["train_loss"].append(train_loss)
        history["val_loss"].append(val_loss)
        history["train_acc"].append(train_acc)
        history["val_acc"].append(val_acc)

        print(f"epoch {epoch+1}: train loss {train_loss:.4f}, train acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
              f"val loss {val_loss:.4f}, val acc {val_acc:.4f}")

    return model, history

print("Training Function v2 Defined.")

        "model": trained_model,
        "history": history,
        "config": config
    }

    # save each config's weights separately

def train_model_early_stop(model, train_loader, val_loader, device, max_epochs, lr, optimizer_name, patience=3):
    model = model.to(device)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    if optimizer_name == "adam":
        optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)
    elif optimizer_name == "sgd":
        optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=lr, momentum=0.9)

    history = {"train_loss": [], "val_loss": [], "train_acc": [], "val_acc": []}
    best_val_loss = float("inf")
    epochs_no_improve = 0

    for epoch in range(max_epochs):
        model.train()
        running_loss = 0.0
        correct = 0
        total = 0

        for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"epoch {epoch+1}/{max_epochs} train"):
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            total += labels.size(0)

        train_loss = running_loss / total
        train_acc = correct / total

        model.eval()
        val_running_loss = 0.0
        val_correct = 0
        val_total = 0

        with torch.no_grad():
            for images, labels in val_loader:
                images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
                outputs = model(images)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

                val_running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
                _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
                val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
                val_total += labels.size(0)

        val_loss = val_running_loss / val_total
        val_acc = val_correct / val_total

        history["train_loss"].append(train_loss)
        history["val_loss"].append(val_loss)
        history["train_acc"].append(train_acc)
        history["val_acc"].append(val_acc)

        print(f"epoch {epoch+1}: train loss {train_loss:.4f}, train acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
              f"val loss {val_loss:.4f}, val acc {val_acc:.4f}")

        # early stopping check
        if val_loss < best_val_loss:
            best_val_loss = val_loss
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            torch.save(model.state_dict(), "models/improved_cnn_best.pth")
        else:
            epochs_no_improve += 1
            if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                print(f"early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
                break

    return model, history

Attempt 3 at Improved CNN by Fixing the Architecture¶

In [24]:
class ImprovedCNNv2(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=4, dropout_rate=0.3):
        super(ImprovedCNNv2, self).__init__()

        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(16)
        self.pool1 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(32)
        self.pool2 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.pool3 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        # added fourth block for more depth
        self.conv4 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm2d(128)
        self.pool4 = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)

        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)

        # global average pooling collapses each channel to a single value
        # this replaces the huge flatten + dense layer, cutting parameters drastically
        self.gap = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)

        # fc layer now only takes 128 inputs instead of 50176
        self.fc = nn.Linear(128, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool1(self.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x))))
        x = self.pool2(self.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x))))
        x = self.pool3(self.relu(self.bn3(self.conv3(x))))
        x = self.pool4(self.relu(self.bn4(self.conv4(x))))

        x = self.gap(x)  # shape becomes (batch, 128, 1, 1)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)  # flatten to (batch, 128)

        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.fc(x)

        return x

print("Improved CNN v2 Architecture Defined.")

from sklearn.metrics import f1_score

def val_macro_f1(model, val_loader, device):
    model.eval()
    preds, labels = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for images, lbls in val_loader:
            images = images.to(device)
            out = model(images)
            _, p = torch.max(out, 1)
            preds.extend(p.cpu().numpy())
            labels.extend(lbls.numpy())
    return f1_score(labels, preds, average="macro")

def train_model_v5(model, train_loader, val_loader, device, max_epochs, lr,
                   optimizer_name, patience, weight_decay=0.0,
                   class_weights=None, min_epoch=3,
                   label_smoothing=0.0,
                   save_path="models/improved_cnn_final.pth"):
    model = model.to(device)

    # weighted loss so the minority classes are not ignored after the merge
    # label smoothing stops the model becoming over-confident on training drivers
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=class_weights, label_smoothing=label_smoothing)

    if optimizer_name == "adam":
        optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=weight_decay)
    elif optimizer_name == "sgd":
        optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=lr, momentum=0.9, weight_decay=weight_decay)

    # sgd at a fixed lr of 0.01 made validation accuracy oscillate badly
    # cosine annealing decays the lr so the model settles instead of bouncing
    scheduler = optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=max_epochs)

    history = {"train_loss": [], "val_loss": [], "train_acc": [], "val_acc": []}
    best_val_acc = 0.0
    best_val_f1 = 0.0
    epochs_no_improve = 0

    for epoch in range(max_epochs):
        model.train()
        running_loss = 0.0
        correct = 0
        total = 0

        for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"epoch {epoch+1}/{max_epochs} train"):
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            outputs = model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            total += labels.size(0)

        train_loss = running_loss / total
        train_acc = correct / total

        model.eval()
        val_running_loss = 0.0
        val_correct = 0
        val_total = 0

        with torch.no_grad():
            for images, labels in val_loader:
                images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
                outputs = model(images)
                loss = criterion(outputs, labels)

                val_running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
                _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
                val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
                val_total += labels.size(0)

        val_loss = val_running_loss / val_total
        val_acc = val_correct / val_total

        history["train_loss"].append(train_loss)
        history["val_loss"].append(val_loss)
        history["train_acc"].append(train_acc)
        history["val_acc"].append(val_acc)

        scheduler.step()

        print(f"epoch {epoch+1}: train loss {train_loss:.4f}, train acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
              f"val loss {val_loss:.4f}, val acc {val_acc:.4f}, lr {scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]:.5f}")

        # checkpoint on macro f1, not raw accuracy
        # raw accuracy let the model win an epoch where one class was dead
        # macro f1 only rewards epochs where all four classes are alive
        if epoch + 1 < min_epoch:
            print("  -> warmup, not eligible for checkpoint yet")
            continue

        current_f1 = val_macro_f1(model, val_loader, device)

        if current_f1 > best_val_f1:
            best_val_f1 = current_f1
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            torch.save(model.state_dict(), save_path)
            print(f"  -> new best model saved (macro_f1={current_f1:.4f}, val_acc={val_acc:.4f}, epoch {epoch+1})")
        else:
            epochs_no_improve += 1
            if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                print(f"early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
                break

    return model, history

print("Training function v5 defined: weighted loss, cosine annealing, warmup checkpointing.")

Training function v5 defined: weighted loss, cosine annealing, warmup checkpointing.

Improved CNN v3: Increasing Network Depth¶

The v2 architecture used four convolutional layers and reached a validation accuracy in the mid sixties, but its training accuracy climbed considerably higher, which indicated that the network was fitting the training drivers more closely than it was learning generalisable features.

Rather than regularise further, this version tests whether the model was simply too shallow to represent the differences between the four behaviour groups. v3 uses nine convolutional layers arranged as two 3x3 convolutions per block for the first four blocks. Stacking two small convolutions covers the same receptive field as a single larger kernel while using fewer parameters and adding an extra non linearity between them.

Channel widths were kept deliberately modest so that the added depth did not simply supply more capacity for memorisation. Label smoothing of 0.1 was also introduced, which discourages the network from becoming overly confident on the training set. All other settings, including the optimiser, learning rate, dropout rate, weight decay and class weights, were held identical to v2 so that the effect of depth could be isolated.

Adding the deeper architecture¶

In [32]:
class ImprovedCNNv3(nn.Module):
    """
    Deeper version of ImprovedCNNv2.

    v2 used four convolutional layers. v3 uses nine, arranged as two 3x3
    convolutions per block for the first four blocks. Stacking two small
    convolutions gives the same receptive field as one larger kernel but
    with fewer parameters and an extra non-linearity in between.

    Channel widths are kept deliberately modest so that adding depth does
    not simply hand the network more capacity to memorise training drivers,
    which was the failure mode observed in v2.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_classes=4, dropout_rate=0.5):
        super(ImprovedCNNv3, self).__init__()

        def block(in_ch, out_ch, double=True):
            layers = [
                nn.Conv2d(in_ch, out_ch, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(out_ch),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            ]
            if double:
                layers += [
                    nn.Conv2d(out_ch, out_ch, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(out_ch),
                    nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
                ]
            layers.append(nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2))
            return nn.Sequential(*layers)

        self.block1 = block(3, 16)      # 224 -> 112
        self.block2 = block(16, 32)     # 112 -> 56
        self.block3 = block(32, 64)     # 56  -> 28
        self.block4 = block(64, 96)     # 28  -> 14
        self.block5 = block(96, 128, double=False)  # 14 -> 7

        self.gap = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(128, num_classes)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.block1(x)
        x = self.block2(x)
        x = self.block3(x)
        x = self.block4(x)
        x = self.block5(x)

        x = self.gap(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x

Model 3 - Fine-Tuning Pretrained CNN (ResNet18)¶

Loading Pretrained ResNet18 and Modifying for 10 Classes¶

In [35]:
# loading resnet18 pretrained on imagenet
# replacing the final fully connected layer with one that outputs 10 classes
resnet_model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)

# freezing all layers initially, only training the new classification head first
for param in resnet_model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False

# replacing the final fc layer as the original resnet18 fc outputs 1000 classes (imagenet)
# we replace it with one that outputs 10 classes (our driver behaviour classes)
num_features = resnet_model.fc.in_features
resnet_model.fc = nn.Linear(num_features, 10)

print("ResNet18 loaded with pretrained imagenet weights.")
print(f"Final FC Layer: {num_features} Inputs -> 10 outputs")

# confirming only the new fc layer is trainable at this stage
trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in resnet_model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in resnet_model.parameters())
print(f"\nTrainable Parameters: {trainable_params:,} / {total_params:,}")

Phase 1: Training Classification Head Only (with 5 epochs)¶

In [36]:
device = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")

resnet_model = resnet_model.to(device)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

# phase 1: only training the new fc head, with backbone frozen
optimizer_phase1 = optim.Adam(resnet_model.fc.parameters(), lr=0.001)

history_phase1 = {"Train_Loss": [], "Val_Loss": [], "Train_Acc": [], "Val_Acc": []}

print("Phase 1: Training Classification Head Only (since backbone is frozen).")

for epoch in range(5):
    resnet_model.train()
    running_loss = 0.0
    correct = 0
    total = 0

    for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"Epoch {epoch+1}/5 Train"):
        images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
        optimizer_phase1.zero_grad()
        outputs = resnet_model(images)
        loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer_phase1.step()

        running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
        _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
        correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
        total += labels.size(0)

    train_loss = running_loss / total
    train_acc = correct / total

    resnet_model.eval()
    val_loss = 0.0
    val_correct = 0
    val_total = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for images, labels in val_loader:
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
            outputs = resnet_model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            val_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            val_total += labels.size(0)

    val_loss /= val_total
    val_acc = val_correct / val_total

    history_phase1["Train_Loss"].append(train_loss)
    history_phase1["Val_Loss"].append(val_loss)
    history_phase1["Train_Acc"].append(train_acc)
    history_phase1["Val_Acc"].append(val_acc)

    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}: Train Loss {train_loss:.4f}, Train Acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
          f"Val Loss {val_loss:.4f}, Val Acc {val_acc:.4f}")

print("\nPhase 1 complete.")

Phase 2: Fine-Tuning Full Network without backbone¶

In [38]:
# phase 2: fine-tuning the entire network with a very small learning rate to not destroy the imagenet features
optimizer_phase2 = optim.Adam(resnet_model.parameters(), lr=0.0001)

history_phase2 = {"Train_Loss": [], "Val_Loss": [], "Train_Acc": [], "Val_Acc": []}
best_val_acc = 0.0
epochs_no_improve = 0
patience = 5

print("Phase 2: Fine-tuning full network (with backbone unfrozen).")

for epoch in range(10):
    resnet_model.train()
    running_loss = 0.0
    correct = 0
    total = 0

    for images, labels in tqdm(train_loader, desc=f"Epoch {epoch+1}/10 Train"):
        images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
        optimizer_phase2.zero_grad()
        outputs = resnet_model(images)
        loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer_phase2.step()

        running_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
        _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
        correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
        total += labels.size(0)

    train_loss = running_loss / total
    train_acc = correct / total

    resnet_model.eval()
    val_loss = 0.0
    val_correct = 0
    val_total = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for images, labels in val_loader:
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
            outputs = resnet_model(images)
            loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
            val_loss += loss.item() * images.size(0)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            val_correct += (predicted == labels).sum().item()
            val_total += labels.size(0)

    val_loss /= val_total
    val_acc = val_correct / val_total

    history_phase2["Train_Loss"].append(train_loss)
    history_phase2["Val_Loss"].append(val_loss)
    history_phase2["Train_Acc"].append(train_acc)
    history_phase2["Val_Acc"].append(val_acc)

    print(f"epoch {epoch+1}: Train Loss {train_loss:.4f}, Train Acc {train_acc:.4f}, "
          f"Val Loss {val_loss:.4f}, Val Acc {val_acc:.4f}")

    if val_acc > best_val_acc:
        best_val_acc = val_acc
        epochs_no_improve = 0
        torch.save(resnet_model.state_dict(), "models/resnet18_finetuned.pth")
        print(f"  -> New Best Model Saved (Val_Acc={val_acc:.4f})")
    else:
        epochs_no_improve += 1
        if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
            print(f"Early stopping triggered at epoch {epoch+1}")
            break

print(f"\nPhase 2 Complete.")
print(f"Best Validation Accuracy: {best_val_acc:.4f}")

Model Evaluation and Comparison¶

Reusable Evaluation Function¶

In [40]:
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix
import seaborn as sns

class_names = [
    "Safe / Talking",
    "Using Phone",
    "Distracted Driving",
    "Reaching / Grooming"
]

def evaluate_model(model, test_loader, device, model_name):
    model.eval()
    all_preds = []
    all_labels = []

    with torch.no_grad():
        for images, labels in test_loader:
            images, labels = images.to(device), labels.to(device)
            outputs = model(images)
            _, predicted = torch.max(outputs, 1)
            all_preds.extend(predicted.cpu().numpy())
            all_labels.extend(labels.cpu().numpy())

    # classification report
    print(f"Model: {model_name}")

    print(classification_report(all_labels, all_preds, target_names=class_names))

    # confusion matrix
    cm = confusion_matrix(all_labels, all_preds)
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
    sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues",
                xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names)
    plt.title(f"{model_name} - confusion matrix")
    plt.ylabel("True Label")
    plt.xlabel("Predicted Label")
    plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f"outputs/{model_name.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_confusion_matrix.png")
    plt.show()

    return all_preds, all_labels

print("Evaluation Function Defined.")

Evaluation Function Defined.

Interactive Demo UI¶

Two interfaces have been created for real-time inference using the best-performing model (ResNet18 Fine-tuned, 88.23% test accuracy):

In-Notebook Widget¶

An ipywidgets-based interface embedded directly in this notebook. Upload any driver image and click Predict to classify it. Results display the top prediction and a top-3 confidence bar chart inline. Preprocessing matches the validation and test pipeline exactly — 224×224 resize and ImageNet normalisation, no augmentation applied at inference time.

Standalone Web Application¶

A Flask-based web application (Development/app.py) with a custom dark-themed frontend (Development/templates/index.html).

Both use identical preprocessing to the training pipeline.¶

In-notebook UI¶

In [44]:
import ipywidgets as widgets
from IPython.display import display, clear_output
from PIL import Image
import io

# transformimg (same as val/test with no augmentation)
infer_transform = transforms.Compose([
    transforms.Resize((224, 224)),
    transforms.ToTensor(),
    transforms.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406],
                         std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225])
])

# confidence bar helper
def make_conf_bar(confidence, label):
    bar_len = 40
    filled = int(bar_len * confidence / 100)
    bar = "█" * filled + "░" * (bar_len - filled)
    return f"[{bar}] {confidence:.1f}%  →  {label}"

# running inference on a pil image
def predict_image(pil_img, model, device):
    model.eval()
    tensor = infer_transform(pil_img).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model(tensor)
        probs = torch.softmax(outputs, dim=1)[0]
    top3_conf, top3_idx = torch.topk(probs, 3)
    return top3_idx.cpu().numpy(), top3_conf.cpu().numpy()

# widgets
upload_btn = widgets.FileUpload(
    accept=".jpg,.jpeg,.png",
    multiple=False,
    description="Upload Image",
    layout=widgets.Layout(width="200px")
)

run_btn = widgets.Button(
    description="Predict",
    button_style="primary",
    layout=widgets.Layout(width="120px")
)

clear_btn = widgets.Button(
    description="Clear",
    button_style="warning",
    layout=widgets.Layout(width="120px")
)

out = widgets.Output()

title = widgets.HTML("<h3 style='margin:0 0 10px 0'>Driver Behaviour Detection with ResNet18</h3>")
hint = widgets.HTML("<p style='color:gray; font-size:0.85em'>Upload a driver image, then click predict.</p>")

# callbacks 
def on_predict(b):
    with out:
        clear_output(wait=True)
        if not upload_btn.value:
            print("Please upload an image first.")
            return

        # reading uploaded file
        uploaded = upload_btn.value[0]
        img_bytes = uploaded["content"]
        pil_img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(img_bytes)).convert("RGB")

        # running inference
        top3_idx, top3_conf = predict_image(pil_img, resnet_eval, device)

        # displaying image + results side by side
        fig, (ax_img, ax_bar) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4),
                                               gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1.4]})

        ax_img.imshow(pil_img)
        ax_img.axis("Off")
        ax_img.set_title("Uploaded Image", fontsize=11)

        # bar chart of top 3 predictions
        labels_top3 = [class_names[i] for i in top3_idx]
        confs_top3  = top3_conf * 100
        colors = ["#2196F3", "#90CAF9", "#BBDEFB"]
        bars = ax_bar.barh(labels_top3[::-1], confs_top3[::-1], color=colors[::-1])
        ax_bar.set_xlim(0, 100)
        ax_bar.set_xlabel("Confidence (%)")
        ax_bar.set_title("Top 3 Predictions", fontsize=11)
        for bar, conf in zip(bars, confs_top3[::-1]):
            ax_bar.text(bar.get_width() + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
                        f"{conf:.1f}%", va="center", fontsize=10)

        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig("outputs/notebook_demo_result.png", dpi=100)
        plt.show()

        print(f"\nPrediction:  {class_names[top3_idx[0]].upper()}")
        print(f"Confidence:  {top3_conf[0]*100:.1f}%\n")
        for i in range(3):
            print(make_conf_bar(top3_conf[i]*100, class_names[top3_idx[i]]))

def on_clear(b):
    upload_btn.value = ()
    with out:
        clear_output()

run_btn.on_click(on_predict)
clear_btn.on_click(on_clear)

# layout 
btn_row = widgets.HBox([run_btn, clear_btn], layout=widgets.Layout(gap="10px"))
ui = widgets.VBox([title, hint, upload_btn, btn_row, out],
                  layout=widgets.Layout(padding="15px", border="1px solid #ddd",
                                        border_radius="8px", width="700px"))
display(ui)

VBox(children=(HTML(value="<h3 style='margin:0 0 10px 0'>Driver Behaviour Detection with ResNet18</h3>"), HTML…

Conclusion¶

This project developed and evaluated a distracted driver classification pipeline using the State Farm Distracted Driver Detection dataset. The original ten classes were grouped into four behaviour categories based on the type of distraction rather than the exact pose, which reflects how a driver monitoring system would categorise risk in practice and removes several pairs of classes that were almost visually identical.

A driver aware split was implemented using GroupShuffleSplit so that no driver appears in more than one of the training, validation and test sets. Every result below is therefore measured on drivers the models have never seen.

Model Test Accuracy Macro F1
Baseline CNN 69.40% 0.6664
Improved CNN v2 63.84% 0.6260
Improved CNN v3 86.00% 0.8600
ResNet18 Fine-tuned 87.24% 0.8682

The baseline CNN provided a reference point but showed a wide gap between training and validation accuracy. The v2 architecture introduced batch normalisation, global average pooling, dropout, weight decay, class weighting and a cosine annealing schedule, and although these changes kept all four classes active, they did not close that gap.

The decisive change was depth. The v3 architecture, using nine convolutional layers instead of four, reached 86.00% test accuracy with a macro F1 of 0.86, placing it within roughly one point of the fine tuned ResNet18 while using 322,836 parameters against ResNet's eleven million. This indicates that the earlier shortfall was caused by insufficient representational depth rather than by a limit in the data.

ResNet18 remained the strongest model at 87.24%, and it reached that level in ten epochs of fine tuning compared with the twenty five epochs and considerably heavier regularisation required by v3. The main advantage of transfer learning on this task is therefore efficiency rather than a higher achievable ceiling.

The best performing model was deployed in two interfaces, an in notebook ipywidgets tool and a standalone Flask web application, both performing inference on uploaded images using the same preprocessing as the evaluation pipeline.

# the classification head was left at ten units when the classes were merged
# only the first four outputs ever received gradient, so the remaining six are
# discarded here to produce a clean four class checkpoint
sd = torch.load("models/resnet18_finetuned.pth", map_location="cpu")

sd["fc.weight"] = sd["fc.weight"][:4]
sd["fc.bias"]   = sd["fc.bias"][:4]

torch.save(sd, "models/resnet18_finetuned_4class.pth")

check = torch.load("models/resnet18_finetuned_4class.pth", map_location="cpu")
print("fc weight shape:", check["fc.weight"].shape)
print("fc bias shape:  ", check["fc.bias"].shape)

fc weight shape: torch.Size([4, 512])
fc bias shape:   torch.Size([4])
